concepts.title: Harappan Urban Planning
concepts.definition: Mature Harappan cities were built of standardized baked bricks whose length and breadth were multiples of the height, laid in interlocking patterns; the citadel rose to the west of the lower town, and covered drains along the streets carried waste out of every house.
concepts.key_idea: Uniform brick ratios and planned drainage across distant sites prove a shared building culture rather than isolated towns.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs101.txt drainage, bricks and citadel-lower town sections
question_patterns: describe the drainage system of Harappan cities
what was the standard ratio of Harappan bricks
differentiate the citadel from the lower town
why were bricks standardized across sites
how were wells and reservoirs managed at Mohenjodaro
what do house remains show about privacy norms

solution_steps.explain: citadel west, lower town east, both walled on mud-brick platforms
length four times and breadth twice the height gave strong interlocking bonds
house drains slotted into street drains kept cities remarkably clean

concepts.title: Seals, Script and Crafts
concepts.definition: Harappan craftsmen cut seals of steatite, made beads of carnelian and faience, and worked copper and bronze; the pictographic script on seals remains undeciphered, and cubical chert weights followed a binary-decimal system of measurement.
concepts.key_idea: Seals carried animals and an unread script, serving as identity and quality markers in exchange networks we can see but not yet read.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs101.txt seals, undeciphered script and weights sections
question_patterns: what materials were Harappan seals made of

describe the weight system of the Harappans

identify the craft products of Chanhudaro
how do seals help archaeologists reconstruct exchange

solution_steps.explain: steatite seals, carnelian beads, faience ornaments and copper tools were mass crafts
short inscriptions with no bilingual key have kept the script undeciphered
cubical chert weights in binary and decimal steps measured goods precisely

concepts.title: Subsistence and Long-distance Trade
concepts.definition: Harappans grew wheat, barley, lentil, chickpea and millets, herded cattle, sheep and goats, and procured raw materials from near and far - copper from Oman and Rajasthan, gold from Karnataka, lapis from Shortughai - with Mesopotamian texts mentioning Dilmun, Magan and Meluhha.
concepts.key_idea: Deposits of imported materials and Mesopotamian references together prove the Harappan world was tied into a long-distance exchange network.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs101.txt subsistence strategies, procuring materials and contact with distant lands
question_patterns: list the crops and animals of Harappan subsistence

solution_steps.explain: copper, gold, lapis and shell travelled hundreds of kilometres to reach workshops
Meluhha in Mesopotamian records matches Harappan goods like carnelian and seals
colonies like Shortughai secured sources of lapis far beyond the alluvium

concepts.title: The End of the Harappan Civilisation
concepts.definition: By c. 1900 BCE most Mature Harappan sites were abandoned; scholars debate causes - climate change, deforestation, excessive floods, shifting or drying rivers and the breakdown of trade - and favour multiple overlapping causes over a single explanation.
concepts.key_idea: The disappearance of seals, script, weights and the distinctive pottery marks the end of the civilisation more surely than any single catastrophe.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs101.txt evidence of an end and multiple causes debates
question_patterns: when did the Mature Harappan culture end

solution_steps.explain: climate, deforestation, floods, river shifts and trade breakdown are the debated causes
the loss of urban traits, not the people, defines the end

concepts.title: Harappan Chronology
concepts.definition: The Mature Harappan culture, with its cities, seals and standardised bricks, is dated between about 2600 BCE and 1900 BCE; subtracting the end date from the beginning gives the length of the mature urban phase.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the end date BCE from the start date BCE yields the duration of the Mature Harappan phase in years.
